text:
maya: quick check — after the q4f16 kernel sweep, do we still want to target 24 GPUs for the eu-west dedicated slab or bump to 30 for runway? :thinking_face:
akshay: short answer: probably +20% headroom. results from the last run show 1.8x bursts in evenings for EU, and our p99 warms up worse on H100 when kernel falls back.
liam: dropping some numbers: avg throughput per H100 (65B q4f16, kernel v2): 220 tokens/s, p99 latency ~ 310ms at concurrency=6. A100 is 160 tokens/s, p99 ~420ms at concurrency=6.
julia: is that with KV cache warm? or cold-warm mix?
liam: mixed traffic (30% cold prefixes). warm-only bumps throughput ~1.25x.
maya: good — so if we plan for worst-case mixed, per-GPU capacity ~220 tokens/s for H100. current per-cluster target is 5k tokens/s per slab (service-level).
akshay: math: for 5k tokens/s target, need 23 GPUs (5000/220=22.7). add autoscale buffer: +25% => 29.
julia: but we also need headroom for kernel fallback to slower path when quantization regresses. fallback observed at 7% of requests during the sweep on eu-west. when fallback happens those GPUs behave like 140 tokens/s.
liam: suggestion: aim for 30 GPUs in eu-west slab, set concurrency target 6 on H100, and set autoscale policy to add 6 GPUs at 70% cluster utilization. that gives quick runway for bursts.
maya: can you paste the autoscale config you propose?
liam: sure — proposed snippet:
```
autoscale_policy:
  min_instances: 12
  target_utilization: 0.7
  scale_step: 6
  max_instances: 48
  cooldown: 120s
```
akshay: nit: min_instances 12 seems low for our SLA during business hours. maybe min 18 for eu-west. also consider separate daytime/overnight scaling tiers.
julia: plus, we should set a hard concurrency cap per GPU to avoid p99 explosion. cap at 8 for H100, 4 for A100 in mixed pools.
maya: agreed. ops-bot do we have a quick sim to run with these params?
ops-bot: run submitted: sim/3861234567-eu-west-30gpus-opts. expected duration ~12m. link: https://redwood.internal/sim/3861234567
akshay: while sim runs — thoughts on keeping a small A100 backup pool? cheaper for off-peak throughput, can serve lower-priority workloads.
liam: backup A100 pool makes sense but don't use as fallback for high-SLA routes. routing policy: prefer H100, fallback to A100 only when cluster util > 85% or specific model variants.
julia: kernel choice note: v2 optimized for q4f16 gave latency wins on H100 but regressed on long-seq (2k tokens). for customers using long-context prompts, we should pin to v1 kernels or use on-the-fly kernel-switching by detection.
maya: that's a good point — add a rule: if predicted sequence_length>1024 route to kernel v1 or a different model variant.
akshay: final capacity ask: I'll update Dedicated order to request 30 GPUs for eu-west (H100), 18 GPUs for us-west baseline, and a 12-GPU A100 backup pool in eu-west.
maya: please also update rollout plan: canary 10% traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback on p99 > 20% increase.
liam: add a perf regression test in CI with the same mixed cold/warm workload; fail rollouts if quality regresses >1% on eval set.
julia: FYI the quant team will continue kernel microtuning next week — expect one more patch that might change throughput numbers by ~5-8%. factor that into the runway.
maya: thanks — once sim completes let's reconvene and finalize numbers. ping me the sim link and results. :thumbsup:
